chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who killed a mamlūk. He said: “He must free a slave, fast two consecutive months, and repent to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.رَقَبَةً: a slave person to be freed; the object of manumission in expiation
key_terms.شَهْرَيْنِ مُتَتَابِعَيْنِ: two consecutive months; the specified duration and continuity of the fast
key_terms.قَتَلَ: killed; the act that occasions the legal expiation
key_terms.مَمْلُوكًا: an owned slave; the person who was killed
key_terms.يَتُوبُ: he must repent; indicating repentance as part of the response to the sin
key_terms.يَصُومُ: he must fast; indicating the required act of fasting
key_terms.يُعْتِقُ: he must emancipate; indicating the obligation to free a slave as expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a man who kills a mamlūk according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man who kills a mamlūk, prescribing expiation through freeing a slave and fasting two consecutive months, along with repentance to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It reflects both juridical consequence and moral accountability for unlawful killing.
